content: Aluminum hydroxide/magnesium trisilicate regular strength tablets should be chewed in doses of 2 to 4 tablets by mouth every 6 hours as needed, with a maximum of 16 tablets per day. The safety and efficacy of this medication have not been established. Aluminum hydroxide/magnesium trisilicate can reduce the levels or effects of raltegravir by enhancing gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents and is contraindicated. It is not recommended to use these medications together, even with dose separation. Aluminum hydroxide/magnesium trisilicate decreases the levels or effects of atazanavir by increasing gastric pH, which reduces atazanavir solubility. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Atazanavir should be administered 2 hours before or 1 hour after antacids. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug, as reduced plasma concentrations of atazanavir are expected. Aluminum hydroxide/magnesium trisilicate reduces the levels or effects of baloxavir marboxil by cation binding in the gastrointestinal tract. This interaction should be avoided, or an alternative drug should be used. Baloxavir may bind to polyvalent cations, leading to decreased absorption. Animal studies have shown significantly reduced plasma levels when coadministered with calcium, aluminum, or iron. Human studies have not been conducted. Aluminum hydroxide/magnesium trisilicate decreases the levels or effects of infigratinib by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. If coadministration with an acid-reducing agent cannot be avoided, infigratinib should be administered 2 hours before and after the antacid. Aluminum hydroxide/magnesium trisilicate reduces the bioavailability of misoprostol acid through an unknown mechanism. Magnesium-containing antacids may worsen misoprostol-induced diarrhea. If an antacid is needed, aluminumor calcium-containing antacids are preferred. Aluminum hydroxide/magnesium trisilicate decreases the levels or effects of pazopanib by increasing gastric pH. Avoid coadministration of pazopanib with drugs that raise gastric pH. Short-acting antacids may be used instead of proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) or H2 antagonists, but antacid and pazopanib dosing should be separated by several hours. Aluminum hydroxide/magnesium trisilicate reduces the levels or effects of ponatinib by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Aluminum hydroxide/magnesium trisilicate decreases the levels or effects of sotorasib by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. If coadministration with an acid-reducing agent cannot be avoided, sotorasib should be administered 4 hours before or 10 hours after the antacid. Aluminum hydroxide/magnesium trisilicate reduces the effects of budesonide by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The dissolution of extended-release budesonide tablets is pH-dependent, and coadministration with drugs that increase gastric pH may cause premature dissolution, potentially affecting drug release and absorption in the duodenum. Aluminum hydroxide/magnesium trisilicate decreases the levels or effects of cabotegravir by cation binding in the gastrointestinal tract. Antacid products should be administered at least 2 hours before or 4 hours after taking oral cabotegravir. Aluminum hydroxide/magnesium trisilicate reduces the levels or effects of dabrafenib by increasing gastric pH. Drugs that alter upper gastrointestinal tract pH, such as PPIs, H2 blockers, and antacids, may decrease dabrafenib solubility and reduce its bioavailability. Aluminum hydroxide/magnesium trisilicate decreases the levels of elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Administration of antacids should be separated by at least 2 hours. Aluminum hydroxide/magnesium trisilicate increases the levels of ethambutol by cation binding in the gastrointestinal tract. Avoid administering aluminum hydroxide-containing antacids for at least 4 hours following an ethambutol dose. Aluminum hydroxide/magnesium trisilicate decreases the levels of ledipasvir/sofosbuvir by increasing gastric pH. Ledipasvir solubility decreases as pH increases. Antacid and ledipasvir/sofosbuvir administration should be separated by at least 4 hours. Aluminum hydroxide/magnesium trisilicate reduces the levels or effects of nilotinib by increasing gastric pH. To avoid this interaction, antacids should be administered 2 hours before or 2 hours after nilotinib. Aluminum hydroxide/magnesium trisilicate decreases the levels or effects of omadacycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Multivalent cation-containing products may impair the absorption of tetracyclines, reducing their efficacy. Dosing of tetracyclines should be separated from these products. Aluminum hydroxide/magnesium trisilicate reduces the levels or effects of pexidartinib by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Pexidartinib should be administered 2 hours before or after taking a locally-acting antacid. Aluminum hydroxide/magnesium trisilicate decreases the levels or effects of rifampin. Concomitant antacid administration may reduce rifampin absorption. Daily doses of rifampin should be given at least 1 hour before antacid ingestion. Aluminum hydroxide/magnesium trisilicate reduces the levels of riociguat by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Administration should be separated by at least 1 hour. Aluminum hydroxide/magnesium trisilicate decreases the levels or effects of sarecycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Multivalent cation-containing products may impair the absorption of tetracyclines, reducing their efficacy. Dosing of tetracyclines should be separated from these products. Aluminum hydroxide/magnesium trisilicate decreases the levels or effects of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir by increasing gastric pH. Velpatasvir solubility decreases as gastric pH increases, becoming practically insoluble at pH >5. Administration of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir should be separated from antacids by at least 4 hours. Aluminum hydroxide/magnesium trisilicate reduces the levels or effects of vismodegib by altering its solubility and reducing bioavailability. The effect on efficacy is unknown. Caution is advised when using aluminum hydroxide/magnesium trisilicate in patients with renal failure or those on magnesium-restricted diets. This medication may alter the absorption of other oral drugs by changing gastrointestinal transit time, pH, or through cationic binding. It is classified as Pregnancy Category C, and its distribution in breast milk is unknown.
